\begin{definition}[Binary Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.binaryFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p308-b005}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p144-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b002
}
\label{FABL.binaryFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.χ}
For a real-valued function $f$ on the binary cube and a subset $S$ of its coordinates,
the Fourier coefficient at $S$ is $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$, where $x$
is uniformly distributed on the binary cube and $\chi_S$ is the Walsh character indexed
by $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Orthogonality of Walsh characters]
\lean{FABL.expect_binaryWalshCharacter_mul}
\label{FABL.expect_binaryWalshCharacter_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryWalshCharacter_injective, FABL.χ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The uniform
average over $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of the product of the Walsh characters indexed by $S$
and $T$ is $1$ when $S=T$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$.
The coordinate of $f$ at $T$ in the Walsh basis is its Fourier coefficient $\widehat
f(T)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)(-1)^{\sum_{i\in T}x_i}]$, where the expectation is uniform over
$\mathbb F_2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every $n\ge 0$ and all real-valued functions $f,g$ on $\mathbb F_2^n$, their uniform
average product satisfies $\mathbb
E_x[f(x)g(x)]=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\widehat f(S)\widehat g(S)$, where
$\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}]$ and likewise for $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Probability density]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p144-b007
}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity}
\leanok
A probability density on the Boolean cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a function
$\phi:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ that is nonnegative at every point and has
uniform expectation $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Probability measure from a density]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.toPMF}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b001}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.toPMF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.nonneg}
Given a probability density $\phi$ on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, assign each point $x$
probability $2^{-n}\phi(x)$. These point probabilities define a probability mass
function on the Boolean cube.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\phi$ be a nonnegative function on the $n$-dimensional
Boolean cube whose uniform expectation is $1$, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. The
associated probability mass function assigns to $x$ the mass
$\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\phi(x)/2^n\right)$, where $\operatorname{ofReal}$ is the
standard map from nonnegative real numbers to nonnegative extended real numbers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Expectation under a density]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p157-b003
}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity}
Given a probability density $\phi$ on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and a function
$g:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, define the expectation of $g$ under $\phi$ to be
the uniform expectation of the product $x\mapsto\phi(x)g(x)$.
\end{definition}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho$ be a nonnegative function on the binary cube
$\bbr_2^n$ with uniform mean $1$, and let $g:\bbr_2^n\to\bbr$ be any function. The
integral of $g$ with respect to the probability measure whose density relative to
uniform measure is $\rho$ equals the uniform mean of $\rho g$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a nonnegative function on the Boolean cube
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ whose uniform expectation is $1$, and let

$\varphi$ equals the uniform inner product of $\varphi$ and $g$.

\begin{definition}[Set indicator]
\lean{FABL.setIndicator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b004}
\label{FABL.setIndicator}
\leanok
For a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$, its indicator function is the function that
equals $1$ on $A$ and $0$ outside $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalized subset indicator]
\lean{FABL.subsetDensityValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b004}
\label{FABL.subsetDensityValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.setIndicator, FABL.uniformProbability}
For a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$, define its normalized indicator at $x$ to be
$\mathbf{1}_A(x)$ divided by the uniform probability of $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Density uniform on a subset]
\lean{FABL.subsetDensity}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b004}
\label{FABL.subsetDensity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.setIndicator, FABL.subsetDensityValue, FABL.uniformProbability}
Let $A$ be a nonempty subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The density uniform on $A$ is the
normalized indicator of $A$, giving a probability density on the Boolean cube.
\end{definition}

of the uniform probability density supported on the zero vector of the binary cube is
$1$.
\end{theorem}

singleton set containing the zero vector, evaluated at $x$, equals the sum of all
characters:
$\operatorname{density}_{\{0\}}(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\chi_S(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Convolution on the Boolean cube]
\lean{FABL.convolution}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p030-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p161-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p161-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b003
}
\label{FABL.convolution}
\leanok
For functions $f,g:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, define their convolution at
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ to be $2^{-n}\sum_{y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n} f(y)g(x-y)$, where
subtraction is in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
\end{definition}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be the Boolean cube, and let
$\varphi:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be pointwise nonnegative with uniform expectation
$1$. For every function $g:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$,
the convolution of $\varphi$ and $g$ at $x$ equals both the $\varphi$-weighted
expectation of $y\mapsto g(x-y)$ and the $\varphi$-weighted expectation of $y\mapsto
g(x+y)$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\phi$ be a nonnegative function on the Boolean
cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ whose uniform expectation is $1$, and let $g: \mathbb{F}_2^n \to
\mathbb{R}$. Then the expectation of $g$ with respect to the density $\phi$ equals the
convolution of $\phi$ and $g$ evaluated at the zero vector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Convolution of probability densities]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p030-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p161-b002
}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.convolution}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.nonneg, FABL.convolution, FABL.convolution_apply}
Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be probability densities on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Their convolution
is the probability density obtained by averaging $\phi(y)\psi(x-y)$ uniformly over
$y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ at each point $x$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{5}
Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be probability densities on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube.
Sampling a point according to the probability measure associated with $\phi$, then
independently sampling a point according to the measure associated with $\psi$, and
adding the two points gives the probability measure associated with the convolution of
$\phi$ and $\psi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Probability induced by a density]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.probability}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.probability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.setIndicator}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\phi$ be a nonnegative function on the Boolean
cube $\bbF_2^n$ whose uniform expectation is $1$, and let $A$ be a subset of that cube.
The probability assigned to $A$ is the uniform expectation of $\phi$ times the indicator
of $A$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\phi,\psi:(\mathbb{F}_2)^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be
pointwise nonnegative functions, each having uniform expectation $1$. For every subset
$A\subseteq(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$, the probability assigned to $A$ by the convolution of
these densities is $\mathbb{E}_{y}\mathbb{E}_{z}[\phi(y)\psi(z)\mathbf{1}_A(y+z)]$,
where both expectations are uniform on $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on the $n$-dimensional
binary cube, and let $S$ be a subset of its coordinates. The Fourier coefficient at $S$
of the convolution of $f$ and $g$ equals the product of their Fourier coefficients at
$S$.
\end{theorem}
